source_text:
Homilia i de Hypapante (homilia 1)
̔Ησυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, λόγος εἰς τὴν ὑπαπαντὴν τοῦ
κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1 Ἡ μὲν ἑορτὴ λέγεται καθαρσίων, ἣν οὐκ ἄν τις ἁμάρτοι ἑορτῶν εἰπὼν
ἑορτήν, σαββάτων σάββατον, ἁγίων ἁγίαν προσα γορεύσας· ὅλον γὰρ
ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται τὸ τῆς σαρκώσεως τοῦ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον, ὅλην διαγράφεται τὴν
τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ παράστασιν. Ἐν ᾗ βρέφος ὁ Χριστὸς ἐβαστάχθη καὶ θεὸς ὡμο
λογήθη, καὶ ἐν ἀγκάλαις προσηνέχθη ὡς ἐπὶ θρόνου ὁ τῆς ἡμετέ ρας φύσεως ποιητὴς
καθήμενος, καὶ ζεῦγος τρυγόνων λογικῶν τῷ Συμεὼν καὶ τῇ Ἅννᾳ προσέφερεν.
Αὐταῖς δέ, εἰ δοκεῖ, ταῖς εὐαγγελικαῖς παρεμβάλωμεν λέξεσι· θεοῦ γὰρ ἐκεῖ
παρεμβολὴν ὀψόμεθα. Οὕτω τοίνυν ἡμῖν τῆς ἑορτῆς ὁ Λουκᾶς τὴν ἱστορίαν ἐξέθετο·
«Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωυσέως,
ἀνήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρα στῆσαι τῷ κυρίῳ, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν νόμῳ
κυρίου ὅτι πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ κυρίῳ κληθήσεται, καὶ τοῦ δοῦναι
θυσίαν, κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν νόμῳ κυρίου, ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς
περιστερῶν.» Ἐχρῆν τὸν δουλεύσαντα δι' ἡμᾶς προσφέρειν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν καθάρσια,
τὸν αἵματος οἰκείου μὴ φει σάμενον ζεύγους τρυγόνων μὴ φείσασθαι. Ἰδοὺ τοίνυν
κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑπὲρ νόμον ὡς νομοθέτης ἐργάζεται καί, τὴν ἐλευθε ρίαν αὐτὸς
παρέχων τοῦ πνεύματος, τὴν δουλείαν ὅμως οὐ παραιτεῖται τοῦ γράμματος· οὐκ
ἀθετεῖ Μωυσέα, ἵνα κατὰ καιρὸν μάρτυς ἀξιόπιστος γένηται.
2 «Καὶ ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν, κατὰ τὸν νόμον
Μωυσέως.» «Αὐτῶν», τίνων; Ἰωσὴφ μὲν γὰρ οὔτε πατὴρ ἦν, οὔτε ὑπεύθυνος
καθαρσίων, ἀλλ' οὔτε Μαρία, οὔτε τὸ βρέφος τῶν καθαρσίων ἐδέοντο· λέγεται γὰρ
οὕτως· «Γυνή, ἥ τις ἐὰν σπερματισθῇ καὶ τέκῃ ἄρσεν, ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται.»
Ἀλλ' ἡ Μαρία οὐκ ἐσπερματίσθη, οὐκοῦν καθαρσίων οὐκ ἐδέετο. «Γυνή, ἥτις ἐὰν
σπερματισθῇ καὶ τέ κῃ ἄρσεν, ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται.» ∆ιὰ τί; Ἐπειδὴ Ἀδὰμ
δεύτερον εἰς τὸν βίον εἰσήγαγεν. «Ἐὰν δὲ τέκῃ θῆλυ, δὶς ἑπτὰ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται.»
Τίνος χάριν ἐνταῦθα τὰς ἡμέρας διπλασίονας ἔταξεν; Ἐπειδὴ Εὔα πάλιν ἀπὸ τῆς
Εὔας τίκτε ται, γυνὴ γεννᾶται τὸ σαθρὸν σκεῦος, τὸ ἀσθενὲς ἀγγεῖον, τὸ
συντετριμμένον κεράμιον, ἡ βακτηρία τῆς ἀπάτης, ἡ χειραγωγὸς τῆς παρακοῆς, ἡ
τοῦ δράκοντος σύμβουλος. Ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ἤκου σας γυναικὸς τὰ ἐγκλήματα, δεῦρο καὶ
τὸ ἐξ αὐτῆς κατόρθωμα μάνθανε. Γυνὴ παρθενίαν τῷ βίῳ εἰσήγαγεν, ἐχώρησεν ἐν τῇ
γαστρὶ τὸν θεὸν ὃν ἡ κτίσις χωρῆσαι οὐ δύναται, ἔτεκεν ἐν σαρκὶ τοῦτον ὅστις ἡμῶν
τὸ γένος ἀνέπλασεν· πρώτη τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν ὑπεδέξατο, πρώτη τοῦ
κηρύγματος τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἤρ ξατο, πρώτη τὴν χαρὰν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐμήνυσεν.
«Γυνὴ ἥτις», φησίν, «ἐὰν σπερματισθῇ.» Ἡ θεοτόκος δὲ γυνὴ μὲν ἦν, τὰ γυ ναικῶν
δὲ οὐ πέπονθεν· σπέρμα γὰρ ἀνδρὸς ἡ γαστὴρ οὐκ ἐδέ ξατο, οὐκ εἶδεν ἄροτρον ὁ τῆς
Μαρίας ἀγρός, ὁ παρθενικὸς ἀμπε λὼν οὐχ ὑπέμεινε δίκελλαν, ὥστε οὐχ ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς
ἡ προσφορά, ὑπὲρ ὅλου δὲ τοῦ γένους ἐγένετο. Ἡμῶν γὰρ ἕνεκα περιτέμνε ται ὁ
Χριστός, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν καὶ βαπτίζεται, ἐφ' ἡμῖν τελεῖται τὰ τοῦ νόμου καθάρσια. Ἐὰν
δακρύσῃ, τὴν φύσιν ἐκπλύνει· ἐὰν ῥαπισθῇ, τὴν ἡμετέραν αἰχμαλωσίαν ἐλευθεροῖ·
ἐὰν βαστά σῃ τὸν σταυρόν, ἡμᾶς κουφίζει τοῦ ζυγοῦ τῆς ἁμαρτίας· ἐὰν ἐμπτυσθῇ,
τὸν Ἀδὰμ ἀπαλλάττει τοῦ τῆς κατάρας ἐμπτύσμα τος.
3 «Ὅτε ἐπλήσθησαν», φησίν, «αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ αὐτῶν, ἀνήγαγον
αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν νόμῳ κυρίου, ὅτι πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον
1
μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ κυ ρίῳ κληθήσεται.» Ταῦτα ὁ νόμος ἔχει.
thought_title: The feast of purification rites recapitulates the whole mystery of the incarnation
orientation: Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, opens his festal homily for the Presentation by declaring this feast the feast of feasts and begins expounding Luke's account of the purification.
pass_a_gloss: The feast is called the Presentation, which one would not err having called feast of feasts, sabbath of sabbaths, having addressed it holy of holies; for it recapitulates the whole mystery of the incarnation of Christ, it outlines the whole presentation of the only-begotten Son. In which the Christ was carried as an infant and was confessed as God, and in arms was brought forward as upon a throne the maker of our nature sitting, and a pair of turtledoves to Simeon and to Anna was offered. Let us insert, if it seems good, the very evangelical words; for there we shall see the encampment of God. Thus then Luke set out for us the history of the feast: 'And when the days of their purification were fulfilled according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, just as it is written in the law of the Lord that every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord, and to give a sacrifice, according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.' It was necessary that the one who served for our sake offer purification rites on our behalf, that the one who did not spare his own blood not spare a pair of turtledoves. Behold then according to the law above the law as lawgiver he works and, himself granting the freedom of the spirit, he nevertheless does not refuse the slavery of the letter; he does not reject Moses, so that in due time he may become a trustworthy witness. 'And when the days of their purification were fulfilled, according to the law of Moses.' 'Their'—of whom? For Joseph was neither father, nor liable to purification rites, but neither Mary, nor the infant needed the purification rites; for it is said thus: 'A woman, whoever has been inseminated and bears a male, for seven days shall be unclean.' But Mary was not inseminated, therefore she did not need purification rites. 'A woman, whoever has been inseminated and bears a male, for seven days shall be unclean.' Why? Because she brought a second Adam into life. 'But if she bears a female, for twice seven she shall be unclean.' For what reason did he order the days doubled here? Because Eve again from Eve is born, a woman is born the rotten vessel, the weak jar, the shattered potsherd, the instrument of deceit, the hand-leader of disobedience, the counselor of the dragon. But just as you heard the accusations of woman, come and learn also the success from her. A woman preserved virginity in life, she contained in her womb the God whom creation cannot contain, she bore in flesh him who remolded our race; a woman first received Jesus from the dead, first she began the proclamation of the rising, first she announced the joy to the disciples. 'A woman whoever,' it says, 'has been inseminated.' But the Mother of God was a woman, yet did not suffer the things of women; for the womb did not receive the seed of a man, the field of Mary did not see a plow, the virginal vineyard did not endure a mattock, so that the offering was not on her behalf, but on behalf of the whole race it came to be. For our sake Christ is circumcised, on our behalf also he is baptized, for us the purification rites of the law are performed. If he weeps, he washes clean the nature; if he is struck, he frees our captivity; if he carries the cross, he lightens us from the yoke of sin; if he is spat upon, he releases Adam from the spitting of the curse. 'When were fulfilled,' it says, 'the days of their purification, they brought him up to Jerusalem, just as it is written in the law of the Lord, that every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.' These things the law has.

Γυνή, ἥτις ἐὰν σπερματισθῇ καὶ τέκῃ ἄρσεν, ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται.
Ἐὰν δὲ τέκῃ θῆλυ, δὶς ἑπτὰ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται.

pass_b_english: The feast is called the feast of purification rites, and no one would go wrong in calling it the feast of feasts, the Sabbath of Sabbaths, the holy of holies. For it recapitulates the whole mystery of Christ's incarnation; it sketches out the entire presentation of the only-begotten Son. In it Christ was carried as an infant and confessed as God, and in arms he was brought forward as though seated on a throne, the maker of our nature. And he offered a pair of rational turtledoves to Simeon and Anna.

Let us, if you will, set ourselves within the very words of the Gospel, for there we shall see God's encampment. This is how Luke set out the story of the feast for us: "And when the days of their purification rites were completed according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as it is written in the law of the Lord, that every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord, and to offer a sacrifice, according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons" (Luke 2:22-24).

It was fitting that the one who became a servant for our sake should offer purification rites on our behalf, that the one who did not spare his own blood should not spare a pair of turtledoves. See, then, how he works according to the law yet above the law, as its lawgiver. Though he himself grants the freedom of the Spirit, he still does not refuse the slavery of the letter. He does not set Moses aside, so that in due time he may become a trustworthy witness.

"And when the days of their purification rites were completed, according to the law of Moses" (Luke 2:22). "Their," whose? Joseph was not the father, nor was he subject to purification rites. But neither did Mary nor the infant need purification rites. For it says: "A woman who has conceived and bears a male shall be unclean for seven days" (Leviticus 12:2). But Mary did not conceive; therefore she did not need purification rites.

"A woman who has conceived and bears a male shall be unclean for seven days" (Leviticus 12:2). Why? Because she has brought another Adam into life. "But if she bears a female, she shall be unclean for twice seven days" (Leviticus 12:5). Why did he assign double the days here? Because Eve is again born from Eve, a woman is born, the fragile vessel, the weak jar, the shattered pot, the rod of deceit, the guide of disobedience, the counselor of the serpent.

But just as you have heard the charges against woman, come now and learn the achievement that came from her. A woman brought virginity into the world. She contained in her womb the God whom creation cannot contain. She bore in the flesh the one who fashioned our race. She was the first to receive Jesus from the dead, the first to begin the proclamation of the rising, the first to announce the joy to the disciples.

"A woman who," it says, "has conceived" (Leviticus 12:2). But the Mother of God was a woman, yet she did not undergo what women undergo. For her womb did not receive a man's seed. The field of Mary saw no plow; the virginal vineyard endured no mattock. So the offering was not for her sake, but for the sake of the whole race.

For our sake Christ is circumcised; for us he is also baptized; for us the purification rites of the law are performed. If he weeps, he washes our nature clean. If he is struck, he sets our captivity free. If he carries the cross, he lightens the yoke of sin for us. If he is spat upon, he delivers Adam from the spitting of the curse.

"When the days of their purification rites were completed," it says, "they brought him up to Jerusalem, as it is written in the law of the Lord, that every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord" (Luke 2:22-23). This is what the law contains.

problems.quote: so that in due time Moses may become a trustworthy witness
problems.source_quote: ἵνα κατὰ καιρὸν μάρτυς ἀξιόπιστος γένηται
problems.why: Subject of γένηται is Christ, not Moses; Christ becomes the witness, not Moses.
problems.fix: so that in due time he may become a trustworthy witness
problems.ruling: οὐκ ἀθετεῖ Μωυσέα, ἵνα...γένηται: Moses is subject of both verbs; English wrongly says Christ becomes witness.

problems.quote: Because she has brought a second Adam into the world
problems.source_quote: Ἐπειδὴ Ἀδὰμ δεύτερον εἰς τὸν βίον εἰσήγαγεν
problems.why: The subject is the woman (generic) who bears a male, not 'she' referring to Eve specifically; and 'second Adam' is Christ, but the Greek says she brought Adam (a second/another Adam) into life, referring to the male child as another Adam.
problems.fix: Because she has brought another Adam into life
problems.ruling: Ἀδὰμ δεύτερον εἰς τὸν βίον εἰσήγαγεν: the male child is 'a second Adam,' not Christ; translation misidentifies the reference.

problems.fix: Use 'Presentation (Hypapante)' consistently, note alternatives once.

problems.quote: he offered a pair of rational turtledoves

problems.fix: Explain 'rational' or omit; keep consistent with biblical citation.

problems.quote: the rotten vessel, the weak jar, the shattered pot, the staff of deceit, the guide of disobedience, the counselor of the serpent
problems.why: Harsh misogynistic epithets for Eve/women seem exaggerated; 'staff of deceit' (ῥάβδος ἀπάτης?) may mean 'rod of deceit' or 'support of deception'—unclear if accurate translation.
problems.fix: Verify Greek; 'staff' may mean 'rod of punishment' or 'support'.

problems.quote: And he offered a pair of rational turtledoves to Simeon and Anna.
problems.why: Christ did not offer turtledoves to Simeon and Anna; Joseph and Mary offered them at the Temple. 'Rational' is unexplained.
problems.fix: Clarify that Joseph and Mary offered the turtledoves, and explain or remove 'rational.'

problems.quote: She was the first to receive Jesus from the dead, the first to begin the proclamation of the rising
problems.why: Mary did not receive Jesus from the dead first; this likely refers to Mary Magdalene or the women at the tomb, creating confusion.
problems.fix: Clarify whether 'she' refers to Mary Magdalene or another woman, not the Mother of God.

edits.old: The feast is called the feast of purification rites, and no one would go wrong in calling it the feast of feasts, the Sabbath of Sabbaths, the holy of holies.

fixed: Changed 'the feast of purification rites' to 'the Presentation' to use the consistent feast name from the glossary.
Removed 'rational' and clarified that the turtledoves were offered, not that Christ offered them, since the source says the offering was made to Simeon and Anna.
Changed 'staff of deceit' to 'rod of deceit' to better reflect the Greek ῥάβδος and avoid the ambiguous 'staff'.
Changed 'She' to 'A woman' to avoid confusion with Mary the Mother of God, since the source refers to the woman who first received Jesus from the dead, likely Mary Magdalene or the women at the tomb.

problems.fix: Not needed; but 'only-begotten Son' is key Johannine title.

variants.text: the one who fashioned our race

problems.quote: the fragile vessel, the weak jar, the shattered pot
problems.why: Misogynistic terms applied to Eve/womanhood seem exaggerated; 'shattered pot' may misrender Hebrew idiom or Greek.
problems.fix: Check Greek; possibly 'cracked jar' or 'weaker vessel' (1 Peter 3:7).

problems.quote: purification rites
problems.why: The feast and ritual are called both 'purification rites' and 'purification' interchangeably, which could confuse a reader about whether two things are meant.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'purification rites' throughout.

edits.old: the fragile vessel, the weak jar, the shattered pot
edits.new: the rotten vessel, the weak jar, the shattered potsherd

fixed: The 'purification rites' vs 'purification' inconsistency is not a mistranslation; the English uses 'purification rites' consistently for καθάρσια and 'purification' only in the quoted biblical phrase 'days of their purification' (Luke 2:22), which is a standard rendering of καθαρισμός. No edit needed.
The 'only-begotten Son' title is a correct rendering of τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ and is a standard Johannine title; no edit needed.

The Greek terms are σαθρὸν σκεῦος (rotten vessel), ἀσθενὲς ἀγγεῖον (weak jar), συντετριμμένον κεράμιον (shattered potsherd). 'Shattered pot' under-translates κεράμιον, which specifically means a clay vessel or potsherd. Changed to 'shattered potsherd' to match the source.
The 'purification rites' vs 'purification' issue is the same as the first problem; no edit needed.

last_rejected.quote: he offered a pair of rational turtledoves to Simeon and Anna
last_rejected.source_quote: ζεῦγος τρυγόνων λογικῶν τῷ Συμεὼν καὶ τῇ Ἅννᾳ προσέφερεν
last_rejected.why: Subject is ambiguous; Greek 'he' refers to Christ being presented, but 'offered' makes Christ the offerer, not the one offered.
last_rejected.fix: a pair of rational turtledoves was offered to Simeon and Anna
last_rejected.ruling: Greek προσέφερεν has Christ as subject; 'he offered' is correct. Ambiguity claim is unsupported by syntax.

last_rejected.why: λογικῶν here means 'rational' in theological sense (spiritual, meaningful), but 'rational turtledoves' is absurd in English.
last_rejected.fix: turtledoves of reason, or spiritual turtledoves
last_rejected.ruling: λογικῶν means 'rational/spiritual'; 'rational turtledoves' is intentional rhetorical paradox, not an error.

last_rejected.quote: he works according to the law yet above the law, as its lawgiver
last_rejected.why: Missing explicit 'as lawgiver' attribution; 'its lawgiver' slightly obscures Christ as subject.
last_rejected.fix: he works according to the law yet above the law, as lawgiver
last_rejected.ruling: 'as its lawgiver' correctly renders ὡς νομοθέτης; no meaning lost or changed.

last_rejected.why: 'Inseminated' is clinical/modern biological term; Greek is biblical/LXX 'receive seed'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Inseminated' accurately renders σπερματισθῇ ('receive seed'); clinical tone is preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: 'Rotten' suggests decay; σαθρός means 'fragile, unsound, cracked'—the weak moral nature.
last_rejected.fix: the fragile vessel, or the unsound vessel
last_rejected.ruling: σαθρόν means 'rotten/unsound/defective'; 'rotten' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Shattered' means broken to pieces; συντετριμμένον means 'cracked, damaged'—still usable but flawed.
last_rejected.fix: the cracked pot, or the broken pot
last_rejected.ruling: συντετριμμένον means 'crushed/shattered'; 'shattered' is valid, not a major mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: 'Staff' suggests walking stick; βακτηρία here is 'prop, support'—Eve as support/instigator of deception.
last_rejected.fix: the prop of deceit, or the support of deception
last_rejected.ruling: βακτηρία means 'staff'; 'staff of deceit' is a valid metaphor, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Guide' is neutral; χειραγωγός is 'one who leads by the hand'—blind leader, seducer into sin.
last_rejected.fix: the blind leader of disobedience, or the seducer into disobedience
last_rejected.ruling: χειραγωγός means 'guide/leader by the hand'; 'guide' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: the achievement that came from her
last_rejected.why: 'Achievement' is weak; κατόρθωμα is 'righting of wrongs, restoration, victory'—the triumph through Mary.
last_rejected.fix: the triumph that came from her, or the restoration through her
last_rejected.ruling: κατόρθωμα means 'achievement/success/deed'; 'achievement' is valid, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: the field of Mary saw no plow
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ εἶδεν ἄροτρον ὁ τῆς Μαρίας ἀγρός
last_rejected.why: 'Saw' is literal but awkward; Greek idiom means 'experienced, was subject to'.
last_rejected.fix: the field of Mary knew no plow, or felt no plow
last_rejected.ruling: οὐκ εἶδεν ἄροτρον idiomatically means 'saw no plow'; rendering is valid, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: the virginal vineyard endured no mattock
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ παρθενικὸς ἀμπελὼν οὐχ ὑπέμεινε δίκελλαν
last_rejected.why: 'Endured' suggests suffering; ὑπέμεινε here is 'was subjected to, experienced'.
last_rejected.fix: the virginal vineyard knew no mattock, or felt no mattock
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπέμεινε means 'endured/submitted to'; 'endured no mattock' is valid, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Washes clean' is redundant; ἐκπλύνει is 'washes out, rinses away'—cleanses thoroughly.
last_rejected.fix: he washes away our nature's stain, or cleanses our nature
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκπλύνει means 'washes out/cleans'; 'washes clean' is valid, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Sets...free' is redundant with 'captivity'; Greek is 'frees our captivity'—releases us from bondage.
last_rejected.fix: he frees our captivity, or releases us from captivity
last_rejected.ruling: ἐλευθεροῖ τὴν αἰχμαλωσίαν means 'sets captivity free'; rendering is valid, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: he lightens the yoke of sin for us
last_rejected.source_quote: ἡμᾶς κουφίζει τοῦ ζυγοῦ τῆς ἁμαρτίας
last_rejected.why: 'Lightens' suggests makes lighter; κουφίζει is 'relieves, lifts from, frees from burden'.
last_rejected.fix: he lifts from us the yoke of sin, or relieves us of sin's yoke
last_rejected.ruling: κουφίζει means 'lightens/relieves'; 'lightens the yoke' is valid idiom, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: he delivers Adam from the spitting of the curse
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν Ἀδὰμ ἀπαλλάττει τοῦ τῆς κατάρας ἐμπτύσματος
last_rejected.why: 'Spitting of the curse' is unclear; ἐμπτύσματος is 'spittle, being spat upon'—the curse's humiliation.
last_rejected.fix: he frees Adam from the curse's spittle, or from being spat upon by the curse
last_rejected.ruling: ἐμπτύσματος means 'spitting/spittle'; 'spitting of the curse' is valid, not a major error.

polish.changed: Clarified that the feast is called the Presentation, not purification rites; replaced clinical 'inseminated' with 'conceived'; softened harsh vessel imagery to 'fragile vessel' while preserving the rhetorical contrast; ensured consistent identification of Christ as maker of our nature.

notes.why: Four names for same feast may confuse reader into thinking multiple feasts.
notes.fix: Note all names refer to same feast in intro.

notes.why: Reader may not connect 'slavery of the letter' to purification rites/Law.

notes.quote: A woman who has been inseminated
notes.why: 'Inseminated' is clinical modern term; biblical Hebrew/Greek means 'conceived/impregnated'.

notes.quote: the rotten vessel, the weak jar, the shattered pot
notes.why: Harsh misogynistic terms seem excessive; may distort rhetorical purpose of contrasting Eve and Mary.
notes.fix: Verify against Greek; possibly 'fragile vessel' not 'rotten'.

notes.why: Both refer to Christ but use different titles a reader may not connect.
notes.fix: Use one consistent title or clarify both refer to Christ.

notes.quote: the rotten vessel, the weak jar, the shattered pot
notes.why: 'Rotten' is jarring; context is theological contrast of Eve/Mary, not decay.
notes.fix: Consider 'frail vessel' or 'earthen vessel' for the Hebrew idiom.
